title: Hiring scratchpad — Riley Park (inference runtime)
content:
Quick notes after loop with Riley Park — raw, for internal sync and follow-up.

Context:
- Role: Senior Inference Engineer (runtime/kernel level). Hiring loop condensed (60m coding + 60m systems + 45m culture + 30m ops).
- Candidate background: 6y infra/ML infra, most recent at mid-stage startup; built customized kernels and inference optimizations (claims L2–L3 quantization experience).
- Interviewers: Liam (kernels), Sofia (serving runtime), me (system design + hiring bar).

Initial impressions (high level):
- Communicates well, pragmatic. Comfortable trading latency vs cost.
- Strong intuition around KV cache and batching tradeoffs.
- Claims limited experience with heterogenous GPU fleets (no real multi-region routing ops experience).

Technical deep dive notes (by section):
1) Kernel/optimization exercise (Liam)
- Prompt: optimize attention kernel for short-ish sequences + high token throughput.
- Riley proposed fused matmul+softmax path, mentioned numeric stability fixes and memory reuse across heads.
- Concrete: sketched blocking strategy + showed awareness of bank conflicts on A100-style memory.
- Missed: couldn't immediately name a couple of cuBLAS/cuDNN pitfalls we hit on fp16 transposes (prob just fatigue).
- Score: "4/5" — strong thought process, some gaps on low-level CUDA idiosyncrasies.

2) Serving runtime design (Sofia)
- Prompt: design an autoscaling policy for mixed-latency workloads (chat + embeddings).
- Good: proposed hybrid policy (latency SLA first, cost-aware additive scaling, small buffer pool for bursts). Suggested prefix caching to accelerate chat tail.
- Gaps: naive fallback policy mapping when model variants incompatible; suggested routing by region but didn't have strong strategies for cross-zone KV cache invalidation.
- Score: "3.5/5" — pragmatic but needs more experience with global cache coherence patterns.

3) Ops & reliability (Aisha)
- Discussed on-call: Riley emphasized signal-based runbooks, SLO-based alerts, and a preference for more automated rollback tooling.
- Strong ops instincts: knows how to isolate incidents to model vs. infra vs. config. Has runbook examples at prior company.
- Lacking direct experience with enterprise KMS/HSM integrations which we sometimes need in Private deployments.
- Score: "4/5".

Culture / collaboration:
- Very collaborative, asked good clarifying Qs, not pushy.
- Mentorship: has run mentoring program, gave examples of upskilling junior engineers on FP32->INT8 quant pipelines.
- Fit: aligned with dev-first engineering values.
- Score: "4/5".

Coding challenge outcome:
- Completed core part with working pseudocode; left edge cases undone (memory compaction). Reasonable for allotted time.

Risk areas / unknowns to close in follow-up:
- Real-world experience operating at multi-region scale + cross-region cache coherence.
- Depth of CUDA kernel productionization (benchmarking, profiling, optimizing for NvLink/PCIe).
- KMS/HSM familiarity for Private deployments (policy, key rotation, audit).

Recommendation draft (internal):
- Overall raw score (avg of sections): "3.6/5" — above bar for IC3/IC4? Suggest IC4 (Senior) with focused expectations around kernel productionization and multi-region ops.
- Hire / No-hire: leaning "Hire (preferred) with targeted mentorship plan".
- Conditions: offer contingent on strong reference checks focused on production kernel rollouts and operating multi-region infra. Consider bumping comp if they show deeper CUDA ship experience.

Suggested next steps / action items:
- Technical follow-up: 30–45m deep dive on CUDA/kernel examples with Liam to probe productionized perf tuning.
- Ops follow-up: pair with SRE for a 30m session on cross-region cache patterns.
- References: ask for 2 references who oversaw kernel/infra shipping at prior company.
- Recruiter: Sofia to draft initial comp band and timeline; keep loop open for 1 week.

Notes to self (todo when drafting formal feedback):
- Capture specific quotes/examples Riley used about memory reuse and bank conflicts.
- Add explicit buy/concise reason for mentorship plan in offer doc.
- Flag multi-region ops training as first 3-month objective if hired.

Raw scratch checklist (for candidate packet):
- [ ] Follow-up CUDA deep dive scheduled
- [ ] Ops pairing scheduled
- [ ] Reference requests sent
- [ ] Draft offer terms ready if greenlit

Unresolved questions to raise in sync with hiring committee:
- Do we need someone who already has KMS/HSM experience day-1 for this hire, or can we support ramp with SRE? My vote: can ramp (not blocker).
- What comp band do we want to target vs. open market for IC4 in SFO region? Ask Sofia.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to formal debrief + scorecard once follow-ups complete.

-- Aisha
